etymologies.etymologyHTML: From Middle English pact, from Middle French pacte, from Old French, and its etymon Latin pactum (“something agreed upon”), from pacīscī (“to agree”). Probably a doublet of patio.

definitions.definition: An agreement; a compact; a covenant.
(international law) An agreement between two or more nations
(intransitive) To form a pact; to agree formally.

quote.citation: 1992, John Higley, Richard Gunther, Elites and Democratic Consolidation in Latin America and Southern Europe, page 129:
quote.text: When national elites pacted in Mexico, they pacted to the advantage of the elites as against the masses and also to the advantage of the center as against the provinces.
